Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I) (c. 600 AD)

SEBELYANOS (ሰብልያኖስ) — the unique-to-Meqabyan teacher of the Edomites and Amalekites, identified as a GEʽEZ RENDERING of BELIAR/BELIAL (the Second Temple personification of evil; cf. 2 Corinthians 6:15, Jubilees 1:20, Damascus Document IV.13-19, Testament of Reuben 4:7-11, Sibylline Oracles 3:63-74). Meqabyan preserves the Beliar-as-Antichrist-teacher tradition that runs from Qumran through Pauline polemic through patristic apocalyptic. Sebelyanos reappears at 2 Mq 9:2 as the teacher of Adam's first sin — extending the Beliar-tradition to a primordial-temptation role beyond the second-temple apocalyptic. The name is DIAGNOSTIC for Meqabyan's relationship to Second Temple Jewish-apocalyptic vocabulary preserved in Ethiopian Christianity.

candidates.draft_body:
Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I) (c. 600 AD)

Sebelyanos=Beliar deepening (paired with seed 17:1 Sebelyanos=Beliar identification): the verse develops the Beliar-figure within the narrative. **Beliar/Belial** etymology: Hebrew בְּלִיַּעַל (belial = 'worthless, lawless'); Septuagint renders variously; Christian-era usage treats Beliar as a specific demonic-name. Patristic-Christian reception of Beliar: 2 CORINTHIANS 6:15 ('what concord hath Christ with Belial?' — the unique-NT-occurrence locating Belial as Christ's antithetical-figure); SIBYLLINE ORACLES 3.63-74 (Beliar as eschatological-deceiver); TESTAMENTS OF THE TWELVE PATRIARCHS (Belial as the spirit-of-fornication + spirit-of-anger across the testaments — see esp. T. Reuben 2.1-3.6 + T. Levi 18.12); MARTYRDOM AND ASCENSION OF ISAIAH 1.8-9 + 3.13-4.22 (Beliar/Belial = the lawless-one-of-the-last-times — most extended pre-Christian Beliar narrative). Tewahedo apocalyptic tradition preserves Beliar as a transliteration-preserved demonic-name (alongside Sebelyanos = Sumerian-Babylonian-syncretized form per Horovitz 1905 p. 218). The Meqabyan identification of Sebelyanos=Beliar is one of the few EXPLICIT-DEMONIC-NAME IDENTIFICATIONS in EOTC canonical literature.

Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I) (c. 600 AD)

Sebelyanos=Beliar Christian-reception (continued from 17:6 + seed 17:1): the verse extends the demonic-identification into Christian-patristic reception. Direct parallels: 2 CORINTHIANS 6:14-16 ('what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness? And what concord hath Christ with Belial?' — Paul's antithesis-doctrine); MARTYRDOM AND ASCENSION OF ISAIAH 4.1-22 (Beliar incarnates-in-Nero-Antichrist — the earliest extant Christian-Beliar-Antichrist identification); ORIGEN Contra Celsum 6.43 (Beliar as kosmokratōr); JEROME In Eph 6:12 + Comm. on Daniel 2.7 (Beliar in the eschatological-Antichrist tradition); AUGUSTINE City of God 20.19 (Antichrist-and-Beliar conflation). Tewahedo apocalyptic tradition preserves the Sebelyanos=Beliar-Antichrist identification in the Mäṣḥafä Mäwet (Book of Death) eschatology + Sǝnkǝsar (Synaxarium) saints'-deaths-narratives. The Meqabyan compositional-signature of preserving demonic-names-explicitly is one of the most-distinctive Tewahedo-canonical features (vs the LXX/MT preservation of 'Belial' only via translational-rendering rather than as proper-name).
